findings.text: the control receipt names a mutation other than the one the dispatch declared: the run record's .node.negative_control declares "change the generated partition from rigel to rigel_debug ... the test asserting the partition and the absence of any _debug partition must be observed to fail", while this log's first line and the run manifest record memory="120G" to memory="0" failing the --mem=120G assertion at tests/agent/test_fleet.py:21, so the receipt proves the memory guard and leaves the declared partition guard without an observed refusal - measured here in memory, the declared mutation does flip tests/agent/test_fleet.py:16 and :27 to false, so the guard exists and it is the receipt that answers a different question.

partition="rigel" and the account at :15 hard-code two values that SiteConfig already owns (imas_ambix/agent/profile.py:472 partition, :474 account) and that every other emitter resolves from a site instance (imas_ambix/agent/slurm.py:452-453, imas_ambix/agent/cli.py:2821 and :2826, :3032-3033), so a site-level change never reaches the fleet generator and the fleet's placement is visible to nothing that reads SiteConfig; the account value is not arbitrary - sacctmgr shows iter with QOS normal and no partition restriction beside grpa with the GPU QOS - but no artifact states that reason, so the next reader cannot tell a deliberate choice from a stale one.

the done_when's "carries no finite --time directive" negative is a string comparison that exempts the exact literal the generator hard-codes, so its predicate is agreement with a constant rather than finiteness: measured in memory, an equally unbounded directive spelled --time=INFINITE fails tests/agent/test_fleet.py:28-31, and no input can make it report a spelling the scheduler would refuse.

the emitted "#SBATCH --time=UNLIMITED" reaches the durable record validated nowhere against the scheduler - tests/agent/test_fleet.py:22 compares it to the same literal, docs/plans/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet.html:124 reports the partition's MaxTime=UNLIMITED as cluster configuration rather than as a check of this directive, the run manifest states that no sbatch command was run, and the repository validates generated job scripts this way elsewhere (sbatch --test-only, docs/compute.html:361) - so the one spelling the whole allocation depends on is the one thing no artifact has tried.

the generator pins 120G while the plan's step states 128 GB (docs/plans/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet.html:259); the dispatch narrowed this deliberately, so the code follows its dispatch, but neither the landing comment nor the evidence anchor records the difference and the 120G figure is the third hard-coded resource constant with no site or profile owner.

the submission test asserts the whole CLI output equals "Submitted fleet allocation job 1275000.\n", which pins the message wording rather than the behaviour, so any future change to the message - or the addition of any preceding line - fails a test whose subject is the opt-in submission seam.

ANSWER declared control versus executed: NO, they are not the same mutation. The run's declared control (live/r-20260921T065502703572-fleet-allocation-holder.json, .node.negative_control) mutates the partition to rigel_debug and requires the partition assertion and the _debug negative to be observed to fail; the executed control (negative-control.log line 1, restated in the run manifest) mutates memory 120G to 0 and observed test_fleet_hold_script_requests_bounded_whole_rigel_node fail at tests/agent/test_fleet.py:21. The guard the receipt demonstrates is therefore the memory directive, not the partition trap the plan names as the reason rigel_debug is unusable (docs/plans/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet.html:130-133). The declared mutation would have failed as required - measured by regenerating the script and applying it in memory, tests/agent/test_fleet.py:16 and :27 both flip to false - so the defect is in the control that was chosen and recorded, not in the test. Under the workstation rule that a control receipt's first line repeats the declared mutation verbatim, this log would be refused as a receipt for the declared control.
ANSWER SiteConfig duplication: YES. Two values the generator hard-codes duplicate fields SiteConfig already owns: partition="rigel" (imas_ambix/agent/fleet.py:14) against imas_ambix/agent/profile.py:472 partition, and account="iter" (:15) against imas_ambix/agent/profile.py:474 account. ANSWER unbounded wall-clock spelling validated against sbatch: NO. "#SBATCH --time=UNLIMITED" appears in exactly two places that judge it - imas_ambix/agent/fleet.py:20 where it is written and tests/agent/test_fleet.py:22 and :29 where it is compared to the same string - and nowhere is it or the finished script checked against the scheduler. The run's own record says so: the manifest states "No sbatch command or job submission was run." The plan's MaxTime=UNLIMITED at docs/plans/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet.html:124 is a survey of the partition's configuration, not a check that this directive is accepted. The repository does own an instrument for exactly this - the compute record at docs/compute.html:361 quotes four sbatch scripts that "passed sbatch --test-only (exit 0)" - so this is a missing check, not an unavailable one; the reviewed node's fence forbade running sbatch, which makes validating the spelling the coordinator's step at submission time.

Note for the next reader: the preserved artefact generated-fleet-hold.sbatch is the CLI's printed output (397 bytes) and differs from a fresh generate_fleet_hold_script() call (396 bytes, sha256 961911787e0a66f1...) by exactly one trailing newline; the directive and body content is identical, so the artefact is a faithful capture. The focused gate was not re-run as a suite here; the single named test's predicates were evaluated independently in memory against the merged sources, which is the fact this review rests on.
